item.title: Disturbing New Allegations Against D4vd | Case by Case
item.description: On April 29, prosecutors released a brief outlining their case against singer-songwriter D4vd, who has been charged in the murder of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez. On this episode of "Case By Case," we examine the state's timeline of events, including the allegation that D4vd stabbed Celeste and went to great lengths to cover up the crime. Plus, an update on Nick Reiner who appeared in the same court just hours before D4vd. "48 Hours" correspondent Erin Moriarty and Los Angeles Times crime writer Richard Winton dig into the new details on both stories.

item.title: D4vd Charged with Murder | Case by Case
item.description: Following the discovery of Celeste Rivas Hernandez's remains in a vehicle registered to D4vd last fall, what were the key developments that led to charges this week? On this episode of "Case by Case," we examine all of the new details coming out of the case against singer-songwriter David Anthony Burke, who professionally goes by D4vd. "48 Hours" correspondent Natalie Morales and CBS News chief correspondent Matt Gutman break down what we know so far about Celeste's death and the alleged abusive relationship she had with the singer.

item.title: Trump meets Netanyahu as his threat to resume strikes looms over Iran
item.description: Trump met Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu as the U.S. and Iran held their fire amid work toward a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Deadly Vacations | Case by Case
item.description: Why are so many dream vacations turning into true crime headlines? On the premiere episode of "Case by Case," we examine the trial of Gerhardt Konig, the former anesthesiologist found guilty of attempted manslaughter after a brutal cliffside attack on his wife Arielle in Hawaii. "48 Hours" correspondent Natalie Morales and CBS News chief correspondent Matt Gutman break down the trial's most stunning moments before diving into the chilling trend of headlines about vacations that turned deadly. From the ridges of Oahu to the waters of the Bahamas, we'll follow it all, "Case by Case."

item.title: Trump meets with Netanyahu after Zelenskyy huddle at White House
item.description: President Trump met with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday, immediately after meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, both of whom are in Washington, D.C., for Sen. Lindsey Graham's funeral. CBS News' Olivia Rinaldi and Aidan Stretch have the latest.

item.title: Sneak peek: The Footprint
item.description: ENCORE: A woman is murdered in her home and the pivotal clue at the crime is a bloody footprint her killer left behind. "48 Hours" correspondent Erin Moriarty reports Saturday, August 1 at 9/8c on CBS and streaming on Paramount+.

item.title: People trapped and injured after powerful earthquake strikes Japan
item.description: A powerful earthquake hit southern Japan, seriously damaging a shopping mall where there are reportedly many people trapped and some feared dead.

item.title: Key takeaways as America honors Lindsay Graham's legacy
item.description: Memories of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham were abundant at the U.S. Capitol ceremony honoring the Republican from South Carolina who died unexpectedly in early July. CBS News' Caitlin Huey-Burns reports.

item.title: Thune remembers Lindsey Graham at Capitol ceremony: "I feel his absence every day"
item.description: Senate Majority Leader John Thune delivered remarks at a ceremony honoring late Sen. Lindsey Graham at the U.S. Capitol. Thune said he feels Graham's absence daily and recalled his trips with the Republican lawmaker around the world.

item.title: Senate staffer remembers Lindsey Graham's impact, says he "knew how to speak to people"
item.description: Lee Holmes, a former chief counsel and staff director of the Senate Judiciary Committee who worked closely with the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, joined CBS News to share more details on Graham's work and the legacy he leaves behind.

item.title: eBay settles with couple "terrorized" in bizarre stalking scandal
item.description: eBay has agreed to pay a large settlement after a Massachusetts couple was the victim of a bizarre harassment campaign​.

item.title: Seattle police search for third suspect linked to deadly shooting at festival near Space Needle
item.description: Seattle police are hunting for a third suspect being linked to a deadly shooting at a food festival near the Space Needle. CBS News' Carter Evans reports.

item.title: Vance says Lindsey Graham was "impossible not to like," honors late senator in U.S. Capitol remarks
item.description: Vice President JD Vance honored late Sen. Lindsey Graham, the influential Republican lawmaker from South Carolina, during a memorial tribute in the Rotunda of the U.S. Capitol. Vance said Graham often supported his causes and was an avid persuader among his colleagues.

item.title: Thune says of Lindsey Graham "I feel his absence every day" in Capitol ceremony
item.description: President Trump is delivering a eulogy for Sen. Lindsey Graham, his one-time opponent for the presidency and later, his close ally.

item.title: What is postpartum psychosis, the disorder at the center of Lindsay Clancy's trial?
item.description: A key question in the Massachusetts murder trial of Lindsay Clancy​ is whether postpartum psychosis drove her to kill her three children.

item.title: Can a debt collector sell your account to another collection agency?
item.description: If your debt is already in collections, your next notice could look very different. Here's why that can happen.

item.title: Friend describes last known movements of missing American in Grenada
item.description: American Elizabeth Waddell was last seen on July 22 while visiting the tiny Caribbean island of Grenada.

item.title: Behind the cultural shift and focus on testosterone and masculinity
item.description: Seventy percent of men say their testosterone levels are important to them and 49% feel it is a measure of their masculinity, according to a survey from "Men's Health." CBS News chief medical correspondent Dr. Jon LaPook talks about medical recommendations for testosterone screening while "Men's Health" editorial director Richard Dorment addresses the changing conversations about testosterone.

item.title: William Shatner and daughter Melanie recall fighting stage 4 cancer together
item.description: Actor William Shatner and his daughter, Melanie Shatner Gretsch, recall how they helped each other as they fought stage 4 cancer side by side.

item.title: Paralympian surprises fellow shark attack survivor
item.description: One year ago, Leah Lendel survived a shark attack in Florida and endured a six-hour surgery to reattach her right hand. She tells "CBS Mornings" why revisiting the site of her attack was healing, how she is conquering her fears and is surprised by Paralympian and fellow shark attack survivor Ali Truwit.

item.title: Fauci diaries, released by Sen. Paul, touch on COVID origins, Trump
item.description: Republican Sen. Rand Paul released more than a thousand pages of journal entries from Dr. Anthony Fauci, teeing up what is likely to be a contentious hearing on Wednesday.

item.title: Woman murdered in 1936 and buried under building is finally identified
item.description: Police have finally identified the remains of a woman murdered nearly a century ago and buried beneath a building in Toronto.

item.title: Johnson & Johnson offers $5.5 billion to settle talc lawsuits
item.description: Johnson & Johnson has offered $5.5 billion to settle tens of thousands of lawsuits claiming its baby powder and other talcum powder products caused ovarian cancer, the company says.

item.title: In final debate, Michigan Senate Democrats spar over outside spending
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed and Rep. Haley Stevens clashed on outside spending and electability in their last debate before Michigan's Democratic primary next week.

item.title: Trump asks Supreme Court to step into dispute over mail-in ballots
item.description: A federal appeals court on Sunday left in place a lower court decision that blocked implementation of key parts of President Trump's executive order.

item.title: Savannah Guthrie asks alleged kidnappers to "do the right thing" in new video
item.description: In her Instagram post,​ the "Today" show host said her family had "done our part" and would "never stop looking for" their 84-year-old mother, Nancy Guthrie​, who has been missing since February​.

item.title: Carly Simon reveals Parkinson's diagnosis: "Learning how to live with it"
item.description: Carly Simon, the singer known for 1970s hits like "You're So Vain," announced she has Parkinson's disease and also was treated for basal cell carcinoma.

item.title: Doctors question plan to screen military members for low testosterone
item.description: Doctors raised a range of concerns about a testosterone screening policy announced by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, which is likely to be costly to implement.

item.title: Hegseth requires testosterone deficiency screening for service members over 30
item.description: The Pentagon will now require service members over 30 to screen for testosterone deficiency, and if needed, they can elect to have testosterone replacement therapy.

item.title: COVID-19 vaccines saved nearly 20 million lives in a year, study says
item.description: The researchers say 600,000 more deaths could have been prevented if vaccine roll-out had been more ubiquitous.
